newsitem.title: THAILAND: THAI STOCKS CLOSE UP ON PREMIER MEETING WITH KING.
newsitem.headline: THAI STOCKS CLOSE UP ON PREMIER MEETING WITH KING.

text.p: After a steep fall in the last two consecutive trading days, the Thai stock market closed in positive territory in moderate trade on reports that the prime minister was to have an audience with the king, brokers said.
"The market went up just because of one reason and that was on the prime minister who is to have an audience with the king later today," said Somnuk Chanrasamee of Nava Finance.

The composite SET index was down most of the day and had dropped nearly 14 points by early afternoon. It only edged into the black in the last 20 minutes of trade to finish up 2.72 points at 638.04 on 5.9 billion baht turnover.

Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh is scheduled to meet King Bhumibol Adulyadej this evening. He will be accompanied by Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya and Bank of Thailand Governor Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi.
They were expected to receive advice from the respected monarch or give him a report on the economic situation.

The meeting comes after the government on Tuesday announced drastic measures aimed at remedying the country's ailing economy. The measures were imposed after receiving recommendations by the International Monetary Fund.

The measures included a suspension of 42 troubled finance companies and an increase in the value added tax to 10 percent from seven. To date 58 cash-strapped finance firms have been suspended since late June.

"Investors had received too many pieces of negative news in the past few days. The upcoming meeting (between the premier and the king) should be considered as positive and helped boost the market," said Somnuk.
Although King Bhumibol is a constitutional monarch seen as above politics, he has in the past intervened in times of turmoid. His word is always heeded.
Brokers said foreigners were quite active in the market today.
Foreigners became net sellers after the economic measures were imposed. On Wednesday, their total net selling amounted to 1.3 billion baht.
Several key sectors gained by the close. The banking sector was the most active in terms of value, rising 0.72 percent, followed by the finance sector, which advanced 6.29 percent.
Thai Farmers Bank topped the active list, unchanged at 115 baht. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642
